problem.title: Unpivot Seller Monthly Listing Fees
problem.prompt: A marketplace platform tracks monthly listing fees for sellers in a wide-format table. Each row contains a seller_id and three columns for January, February, and March listing fees (jan_fees, feb_fees, mar_fees). Convert this wide-format data into long format with one row per seller per month. The output must have three columns: seller_id (integer), month_name (text, values 'January', 'February', 'March'), and listing_fee (numeric). Exclude any rows where the listing fee is NULL. Order the final result by seller_id ascending, then by month_name in calendar order (January, February, March). Note: PostgreSQL has no native UNPIVOT; use UNION ALL of SELECT statements, one per source column, each projecting the seller_id, a literal month label, and the corresponding fee column.
problem.schema_ddl: CREATE TABLE seller_monthly_fees (seller_id INTEGER, jan_fees NUMERIC(10,2), feb_fees NUMERIC(10,2), mar_fees NUMERIC(10,2));
problem.example_input_data: INSERT INTO seller_monthly_fees (seller_id, jan_fees, feb_fees, mar_fees) VALUES (101, 50.00, 55.00, 60.00), (102, 45.00, NULL, 52.00), (103, NULL, 48.00, 50.00), (104, 60.00, 62.00, 65.00);

composite_moves: reshape: unpivot three wide columns (jan_fees, feb_fees, mar_fees) into long format using UNION ALL of three SELECTs
row-filter: exclude NULL listing_fee values via WHERE clause in each UNION branch or outer WHERE
sort: ORDER BY seller_id ASC, custom month order (January, February, March) using CASE expression

hints: PostgreSQL does not have a native UNPIVOT keyword; consider using UNION ALL to combine multiple SELECT statements.
Each SELECT in the UNION should project the seller_id, a literal string for the month name, and one of the three fee columns. Remember to filter out NULLs.

Use UNION ALL with three branches: SELECT seller_id, 'January' AS month_name, jan_fees AS listing_fee FROM seller_monthly_fees WHERE jan_fees IS NOT NULL, and similarly for February and March. Order the final result using a CASE expression to enforce January < February < March ordering.
problem.answer_key: SELECT seller_id, month_name, listing_fee FROM (SELECT seller_id, 'January' AS month_name, jan_fees AS listing_fee FROM seller_monthly_fees WHERE jan_fees IS NOT NULL UNION ALL SELECT seller_id, 'February' AS month_name, feb_fees AS listing_fee FROM seller_monthly_fees WHERE feb_fees IS NOT NULL UNION ALL SELECT seller_id, 'March' AS month_name, mar_fees AS listing_fee FROM seller_monthly_fees WHERE mar_fees IS NOT NULL) AS unpivoted ORDER BY seller_id ASC, CASE month_name WHEN 'January' THEN 1 WHEN 'February' THEN 2 WHEN 'March' THEN 3 END ASC;

_meta.scenario: a marketplace platform tracking seller inventory and listing fees

user_solution:
/* notes */
with base as (
    SELECT 
        seller_id,
        'January' AS month_name,
        jan_fees AS listing_fee
    FROM seller_monthly_fees
    WHERE jan_fees IS NOT NULL
    
    UNION ALL
    
    SELECT 
        seller_id,
        'February' AS month_name,
        feb_fees AS listing_fee
    FROM seller_monthly_fees
    WHERE feb_fees IS NOT NULL

    UNION ALL
    
    SELECT 
        seller_id,
        'March' AS month_name,
        mar_fees AS listing_fee
    FROM seller_monthly_fees
    WHERE mar_fees IS NOT NULL
)
SELECT *
FROM base;
